elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Revised Section 6.1 still binds Customer: "the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the 'Deerskin' brand ...". The redline narrows rather than deletes the covenant, so the preferred no-exclusivity outcome is not achieved.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: The open-ended extension "or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled ...)" is deleted; the restraint and the brand exclusivity now run only to "Deerskin Products", a term expressly defined in Section 1.1 (with closeout and Joan Cook carve-outs).

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: "during the term of this Agreement" is replaced by "for a period of twelve (12) months from the Effective Date". Because the period is anchored to the Effective Date rather than the term, the Section 4.1 annual auto-renewal no longer extends the restraint.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "This Section 6.1 shall terminate automatically if HDI fails to meet any service level ... under this Agreement." The exit is self-executing (no notice or cure step) and applies to Vendor. Note the agreement does not itself define a schedule of "service levels"; the trigger is workable because it is tied to HDI's obligations "under this Agreement", but a cross-reference to the performance obligations (e.g. Section 1.6 and any agreed uptime standard) would remove all doubt.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Same added sentence: "... or any delivery date under this Agreement", producing an automatic end to the restraint on any HDI delivery-date failure, which the original clause lacked (Section 1.6 gave only a termination right if the Site was not live in 70 days).

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Not a preferred-level element; assessed under fallback only.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: all four fallback elements (defined category, twelve-month cap, automatic service-level exit, automatic delivery-date exit) appear in operative language in Section 6.1, not merely in the margin comment.
Preferred level is not met and the finding correctly proceeds at the fallback: the covenant on the Company and HDI's exclusive right over the "Deerskin" brand both survive in narrowed form.

Minimality holds. Each edit maps to a selected element: deleting "during the term of this Agreement" and inserting the twelve-month period serves the duration element; deleting "or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar ...)" is necessary to confine the restraint to the defined "Deerskin Products" category; the added sentence supplies the two automatic-exit elements. No survival tail, expense language, cure procedure, damages category or other extra was bolted on.

Favourable retained language is preserved: the "Except as provided in Section 6.2" opener and the closeout-merchandise carve-out are untouched, and HDI's reciprocal covenant in Section 6.3 (which benefits us) is left intact, consistent with the guidance to keep exclusivity that benefits Customer.

Intent is preserved. Section 4.1 term and auto-renewal, the Effective Date definition, and the Section 6.2 exception all continue to operate without contradiction; decoupling the restraint from the term creates no dangling cross-reference and no retained sentence that reinstates term-long exclusivity.

Optional hardening (not required for completeness, and not a defect to repair): "any service level" is not tied to a defined SLA in this agreement. If HDI resists, consider pointing the trigger at identified obligations (e.g. "any service level or delivery date set out in Section 1 or any Exhibit hereto") so the automatic exit cannot be argued to rest on an undefined standard.
